title: Real-time imaging assay of multivesicular body-PM fusion to quantify exosome release from single cells
protocol: Maintain HeLa cells in T75 flask using DMEM supplemented with components.
Remove culture medium from T75 flask, rinse with PBS.
Add trypsin to the T75 flask and incubate until cells detach.
Resuspend detached cells thoroughly in full medium after detaching.
Split HeLa cells 2x a week at a 1:20 ratio.
Seed cells at a density of 25-30% on coverslips or fluorodishes.
Transfect HeLa cells at 50-60% confluency with CD63-pHluorin plasmid DNA.
Dilute 500 ng CD63-pHluorin plasmid DNA in Optimem to a total volume of 100 μl.
Dilute 1.5 μl Lipofectamine 2000, at a ratio of 1:3 with DNA, in Optimem to a total volume of 100 μl.
Add the 100 μl Lipofectamine 2000 solution to the DNA solution, vortex the mixture for 10 seconds and incubate at room temperature for 10-15 min.
Refresh the culture medium of HeLa cells with pre-warmed full medium.
Add the total 200 μl transfection mix dropwise to the HeLa cells and incubate the cells for 6 hours.
Refresh the culture medium of transfected cells with pre-warmed full medium and incubate for another 18 hours.
Place the coverslip with CD63-pHluorin-transfected HeLa cells in the imaging chamber.
Cover the cells with imaging medium.
Place the imaging chamber or Fluorodish on the microscope stage holder.
Focus the imaging plane on the basal plasma membrane of CD63-pHluorin transfected HeLa cells.
Choose an imaging field containing 2 or more cells with average expression levels.
Image at ≥2Hz (2fps) for a time period that allows for proper quantification, typically using an exposure time between 50-300ms.
Maintain focus at the plasma membrane using Perfect Focus System/Adaptive Focus Control.
Use the lowest laser intensity and shortest exposure time possible to avoid phototoxicity.
Image ≥5 different fields.
Load imaging data in ImageJ/Fiji for image analysis.
Count the number of fusion events that occur per minute for MVB-PM fusion rate determination.
Discriminate sudden increases in fluorescence from full MVB-PM fusion by analyzing the fluorescent profile before and after initial fusion.

Consider a burst of fluorescence as an exosome release event if it meets criteria: peak intensity ≥ 1.5-fold above background, reaches peak intensity within two frames at 2Hz imaging rate, has a size of at least 400 nm, shows minimal movement post-burst (less than twice the diameter), and lasts for ≥ 2 seconds (visible in > 4 consecutive frames).
Determine the diameter of the fusion event by drawing a straight line through the event at peak intensity.
Select the ‘Plot Profile’ option under ‘Analyze’ to determine the full width at half maximum (FWHM) of the fusion event.
Draw a circular region of interest (ROI) around the fusion event with a diameter twice the FWHM of the fusion event at its peak intensity.
Select ‘Image’→’Stacks’→’Plot Z-Axis Profile’ to plot the fluorescence intensity profile.
Analyze the data in ImageJ/FIJI or save as .csv for subsequent analysis in Microsoft Excel or GraphPad Prism.
